resolution: The path overlay revealed the routes staircasing and tangling into boxy knots — the grid BFS produces jagged cell paths, worst in the flow-neutral junction/crosswalk blocks where many cars' routes wove into overlapping rectangles. Fixed with a string-pull (line-of-sight simplification) over the lane-centered polyline: each run is pulled taut to the longest straight shot that stays CLEAN — on the road network AND, where it crosses a flowed lane, within half a tile of that lane's centerline. That constraint means a straight lane can't be diagonally cut (cars stay centered per req_2071) while flow-neutral junction/crosswalk blocks (no centerline constraint) straighten freely, collapsing the boxy intersection tangle into clean straight/diagonal crossings. 6/6 traffic tests (the centering test now checks for a centered horizontal SEGMENT, since string-pull collapses the straight run to its endpoints); re-baked + self-shot with the P overlay confirms clean straight lines down the lanes.
